fit: task-based differences between Parkinson visual hallucination groups
assessment: BNA poster P-W082 measures attention-task behavior and fitted drift rate in groups defined by hallucination status. It supplies neither a fig exposure nor a change in symptom frequency.

fit: clinical status subgroup and sensory evidence accumulation
assessment: The peer-reviewed analysis includes 20 Parkinson patients with visual hallucinations, 25 without and 12 controls. Five Parkinson exclusions are documented. This is a linked analysis of the BNA work and offers no fig or episode-frequency comparison.

fit: longitudinal clinical psychosis onset and remission in Parkinson
assessment: The diagnosis can include hallucinations or delusions. Follow-up visits and medication comparisons address clinical diagnoses, without a visual event count or dietary intake comparison.
The primary abstract identifies Rush Hallucination Inventory interviews at four visits over 48 months. The full methods for modality and frequency remain open. No dried fig intake is reported.

fit: visual physiology in Parkinson without reported hallucinations
assessment: Ten Parkinson participants reported no hallucinations. The group comparison records evoked magnetic responses to visual stimuli and provides no edible exposure or clinical visual event rate.

fit: changes in visual and other hallucinations in secondary vascular parkinsonism
assessment: The two case timelines describe secondary rather than idiopathic parkinsonism. Symptoms recurred during unresolved fistula disease and improved after treatment in Case 1. Food intake and visual episode rates were not measured.

fit: Parkinson visual hallucination history across morning motor groups
assessment: Table 2 gives 8 of 20 versus 26 of 72 participants with a visual hallucination history by motor benefit group. This largely overlapping prevalence comparison did not quantify subsequent episodes or test diet.

fit: imaging by visual hallucination status in dementia with Lewy bodies
assessment: Printed OP-367 is a member-level PET comparison. Symptom status and metabolic differences are reported in a different clinical population. No culinary exposure or separate visual episode count was assessed.

fit: larger consortium imaging and visual hallucination status
assessment: The original abstract describes cross-sectional PET comparisons in 171 people with dementia with Lewy bodies. The imaging cohort may overlap with OP-367. No food comparison is described and the full tables are still open.

fit: hallucination presence across Parkinson motor subtypes
assessment: The final-visit motor-subtype comparison records hallucinations without a verified visual modality or episode rate. M255 has the same cohort features. No dried fig exposure is measured.

fit: dried fig mineral presence and separate postmortem Parkinson tissue fractions
assessment: USDA measured the four metals in dried figs. The primary postmortem report distinguishes soluble substantia nigra iron and copper from other fractions without measuring oral intake, uptake, or visual episodes.

fit: open-label apomorphine and visual hallucination severity
assessment: Available primary previews describe favorable severity and caregiver distress changes. The numerical results, follow-up and medicine changes remain unevaluated at original-body depth. The drug infusion provides no dried fig or visual episode rate comparison.
